gloss: to be built, to be constructed

definitions.gloss: to be built, to be erected, to be constructed
definitions.explanation: Used for buildings and structures when they come into existence or stand in a location. An intransitive verb — the building is the subject.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいビルが{建|た}った。
{駅前|えきまえ}にマンションが{次々|つぎつぎ}と{建|た}っている。
examples.english: Condominiums are being built one after another in front of the station.

examples.japanese: この{寺|てら}は{鎌倉|かまくら}{時代|じだい}に{建|た}てられたが、{何度|なんど}も{再建|さいけん}され、{今|いま}の{建物|たてもの}は{江戸|えど}{期|き}に{建|た}ったものだ。
examples.english: This temple was originally built in the Kamakura period, but it was rebuilt many times, and the current structure was erected in the Edo period.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Godan verb ending in つ: {建|た}たない, {建|た}ちます, {建|た}って, {建|た}てば.

USAGE:
An intransitive verb — the building itself is the subject (ビルが{建|た}つ). The transitive counterpart is {建|た}てる (to build something). Do not confuse with the homophone {立|た}つ (to stand up) or {経|た}つ (time passes), which use different kanji.

TRANSITIVITY PAIR:
- {建|た}つ (intransitive): A building is built / stands
- {建|た}てる (transitive): Someone builds a building
